On Tue, Dec 15, 2026 at 09:02 AM Aisha Qureshi <procurement@cobaltbridge.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether Redwood SCIM supports vendor-defined custom attributes and how they are persisted/updated?

Hi Aisha — great questions. Notes from today's walkthrough follow; attached are the artifacts we discussed (redwood_idam_matrix.pdf, scim_sync_flow.yaml). Key answers inline: 

1) SCIM custom attributes and persistence:
- Redwood's SCIM implementation supports vendor-defined schema extensions (SCIM: EnterpriseUser and custom extensions). Custom attributes declared in the tenant's SCIM profile are persisted in the user resource under the extension namespace (e.g., urn:redwood:schemas:User:extension).
- Attribute mapping is configurable in the tenant console and via API. Mappings can be one-to-one or use simple transformations (static value, prefix/suffix, concatenation).
- Bulk operations: our SCIM API supports bulk PATCH for groups and users (RFC7644 bulk) with per-item status and retry headers. For partial failures we return a bulk response with item-level status and an idempotency token for retry. We also expose a webhook for sync failure alerts.

2) Delegated admin and RBAC:
- RBAC model: roles are collections of permissions. Out-of-the-box roles: Organization Admin, Tenant Admin, App Admin, Helpdesk Operator, Read-Only Auditor.
- Scope: roles may be bound to organization, tenant, or application scope. You can create scoped roles such as "Helpdesk Operator (tenant:marketing)".
- Delegated admin: tenant admins can create custom role bindings limited to specific application IDs or user groups via the Console or the Admin API. Audit logs record who granted which role and when.

3) SAML + OIDC support:
- Yes, tenants may enable both SAML and OIDC concurrently. We support multiple IdP configurations per tenant and route auth requests based on URL or identity hint.
- Sample SAML attribute mapping (extract from attached matrix):
  - NameID -> user.primary_email
  - urn:oid:2.5.4.42 (givenName) -> user.given_name
  - urn:oid:2.5.4.4 (sn) -> user.family_name
  - urn:custom:cobalt:costCenter -> user.extension.costCenter

- OIDC claim mapping:
  - sub -> user.id
  - email -> user.primary_email
  - preferred_username -> user.username
  - groups -> user.groups (array)

Attachment: redwood_idam_matrix.pdf (PDF, ~420KB)
Attachment: scim_sync_flow.yaml (text, ~7KB)

If helpful, we'll include a small sample SCIM PATCH payload in the questionnaire response.

Best,
Connor
